items.title: Interactive demo on unvibe.xyz/demo: static, in-browser, replaying the recorded fixture
items.summary: An in-browser demo of the recorded urllib3 review is built for unvibe.xyz/demo, linked from the landing page as Try the demo. It replays the same recordings with the same matcher as the service (now shared), keeps comments in the browser with a Reset demo, and disables Submit and settings.
items.whatChanged: An in-browser demo of the recorded urllib3 review is built for unvibe.xyz/demo, linked from the landing page as Try the demo. It replays the same recordings with the same matcher as the service (now shared), keeps comments in the browser with a Reset demo, and disables Submit and settings.
items.whatToTry: Nothing changes in the installed app beyond the shared replay matcher; the demo goes live on unvibe.xyz with the next release.

items.title: Threads: reply hover controls overlap the first line of text; an empty citation chip renders
items.summary: Reply hover controls no longer draw over the text (a compact toolbar floats beside the first line only); a citation chip can never render empty; each avatar is centred on its own first line (serif AI replies and sans human replies), in light, dark and Studio fonts.
items.whatChanged: Reply hover controls no longer draw over the text (a compact toolbar floats beside the first line only); a citation chip can never render empty; each avatar is centred on its own first line (serif AI replies and sans human replies), in light, dark and Studio fonts.
items.whatToTry: Hover an agent reply in a thread, and look at the end of a reply with citations.

items.title: Extension: Review in Unvibe lands on a bare confirm page; start the review via the worker instead
items.summary: The extension's Review in Unvibe button now starts the review itself and opens it directly, with no confirm page; failures show on the button. Plain /open?pr= links still ask first, on a confirm page styled inside the app.
items.whatChanged: The extension's Review in Unvibe button now starts the review itself and opens it directly, with no confirm page; failures show on the button. Plain /open?pr= links still ask first, on a confirm page styled inside the app.
items.whatToTry: Reload the extension on chrome://extensions and click Review in Unvibe on a PR.

items.title: Release notes inside every build (previews and releases), shown in the app
items.summary: Every build ships its release notes, cumulative since the last release. Settings → Version shows each channel's notes (what updating would bring) behind its Notes button.
items.whatChanged: Every build ships its release notes, cumulative since the last release. Settings → Version shows each channel's notes (what updating would bring) behind its Notes button.
items.whatToTry: Open Settings → Version and press Notes on a channel.

items.title: Diff: turn Hide uninteresting into a level selector (default as today, up to >= substantive), with a hidden-count tooltip
items.summary: The diff Hide menu is an ordered category list (Uninteresting · Mechanical · Routine · Substantive · Needs attention) with swatches, counts and eye icons; clicking a row hides it and everything less important. It hides exactly what you ask: guide-cited hunks are no longer exempt, and clicking a citation to a hidden hunk reveals it. Hunk headers show only the score dot. The button shows an open eye when nothing is hidden.
items.whatChanged: The diff Hide menu is an ordered category list (Uninteresting · Mechanical · Routine · Substantive · Needs attention) with swatches, counts and eye icons; clicking a row hides it and everything less important. It hides exactly what you ask: guide-cited hunks are no longer exempt, and clicking a citation to a hidden hunk reveals it. Hunk headers show only the score dot. The button shows an open eye when nothing is hidden.
items.whatToTry: Open a review diff, hide up to Routine, then click a guide citation that points into a hidden hunk.
items.caveats: Needs attention can never be hidden. The hunk prompt no longer forbids marking cited hunks uninteresting, so newly built guides may hide more. Full gates not yet run.

items.title: Ask threads: drop the redundant comment/Reviewer comment/ask chips (avatars already say who's speaking)

items.title: Chrome extension: Review in Unvibe from GitHub PRs, and a side panel to Explain/Ask about any page with local repos
items.summary: Chrome extension: a Review in Unvibe button on GitHub PRs, and a side panel that answers questions about any page by reading your active repos (repo-qualified citations). Settings → Extension has install help, active-repo checkboxes (default the 3 most recent) and the panel model (default muse-spark). Web-page threads are listed under Documents → Web pages; Reviews shows only PRs and branches.
items.whatChanged: Chrome extension: a Review in Unvibe button on GitHub PRs, and a side panel that answers questions about any page by reading your active repos (repo-qualified citations). Settings → Extension has install help, active-repo checkboxes (default the 3 most recent) and the panel model (default muse-spark). Web-page threads are listed under Documents → Web pages; Reviews shows only PRs and branches.
items.whatToTry: Settings → Extension: Show extension folder, then load it unpacked on chrome://extensions. Open any page, open the side panel, select text and Ask.
items.caveats: Citation click-through to the app comes after v1. The panel page is plainly styled. Full gates not yet run.
